title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
gist: A Sydney team led by transplant surgeon Carlo Pulitano claims to have kept a donated human liver alive at body temperature outside the body for seven weeks on an automated perfusion rig, shattering the prior two-week record. The commercially interesting shift is that long-duration machine perfusion is being repositioned from organ preservation into a platform for human-organ drug testing, gene therapy delivery and even organ multiplication, with startups (Aeternum Life Technologies, Apersys, Bexorg, Altos Labs) and two new scientific societies forming around it.

insights.claim: A team at Royal Prince Alfred Hospital in Sydney led by surgeon Carlo Pulitano claims to have kept a donated human liver alive outside the body for seven weeks under fully normothermic (about 37 degrees C) conditions, with the results not yet formally published.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: An unpublished claim from a single center sets the technical ceiling for organ perfusion; watch for the peer-reviewed paper before underwriting any valuation built on multi-week organ life support.
insights.quote: Our group is the only one in the world to have maintained a human liver under fully normothermic, physiological conditions for seven weeks

insights.claim: The prior record for keeping an internal organ alive outside the body was about two weeks, set in Switzerland several years ago, also with a liver, meaning the Sydney result is roughly a 3.5x step change rather than an incremental gain.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Step-function technical records are what pull capital into a field; the size of the jump is the signal, not the absolute number of weeks.

insights.claim: Automation, not new biology, was the stated unlock: across 55 consecutively perfused human livers, those on the automated control system averaged about four weeks of survival versus the manually adjusted system, a tripling of average survival.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: If the bottleneck is control engineering and sensors rather than biology, value accrues to the hardware/software stack around the organ, a more defensible and faster-scaling asset than a single surgical technique.
insights.quote: the average survival time tripled, to about four weeks
insights.locator: 'Pulitano says the key to breaking the record'

themes.theme: Perfusion economics in today's transplant market

insights.claim: Perfusion is already standard-of-care creep rather than frontier research: Paulo Martins of the University of Oklahoma says about half the kidneys he transplants are now perfused despite the process adding up to $100,000 to the cost of a transplant.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: A six-figure per-case cost that clinicians already accept establishes real pricing power and a live revenue base for perfusion device makers, independent of the long-duration research use case.
insights.quote: about half the kidneys he transplants are now perfused, even though the process can add $100,000 to the cost of a transplant
insights.locator: 'Perfusion has already enabled doctors to restart hearts'

insights.claim: Conventional practice still ships most transplant organs in ice buckets with only a few hours of viability, and switching to warm or cold perfusion roughly doubles the holding window, which is the baseline improvement already monetizable today.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Doubling the viability window loosens geographic matching constraints, the near-term driver of perfusion adoption and of organ-logistics business models.
insights.locator: 'Most organs destined for transplant survive only a few hours'

insights.claim: Perfused organs reportedly begin repairing themselves and strengthening after about a day on the machine, which is the mechanism behind a Swiss team's 2022 transplant of a damaged liver held on perfusion for three days.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Self-repair on the machine converts marginal, otherwise-discarded organs into usable grafts, expanding the transplantable supply, which is the clearest commercial payoff in the near term.
insights.locator: 'Scientists have already discovered possible medical benefits'

insights.claim: Pulitano's startup Aeternum Life Technologies will support a planned Sydney trial transplanting low-quality livers kept on perfusion for four days, a far shorter and more clinically grounded horizon than the seven-week record.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: The commercial roadmap being tested is four days, not seven weeks: the trial-ready product is marginal-organ rescue, and that is the milestone to watch.

insights.claim: Apersys CEO and cofounder Waldemar Hoffmann says peers believe the seven-week record is genuine but do not know how healthy the organ was at the end, and questions whether any surgeon would ever need an organ kept alive for nearly two months.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: A competing operator in the same field framing the record as a solution without a problem is the key bear case: duration records may not map to clinical demand or reimbursable indications.
insights.quote: The key question is what the purpose for a seven-week perfusion would be

insights.claim: The article implicitly separates proven value (hours-to-days perfusion that expands the usable organ pool) from speculative value (multi-week perfusion), with the long-duration claim resting on an unpublished dataset and no end-state organ health data.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Price the near-term, clinically validated perfusion market separately from the long-duration 'organ medicine' option value; conflating them overpays for the latter.

themes.theme: Organs as a research and manufacturing platform

insights.claim: Pulitano frames long-duration perfusion as a human organ model for translational research that no animal system can match, because the biology, immunology and drug responses are human from the start, and says he has already tried adding gene therapies to perfused livers.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: This reframes perfusion from a transplant device into preclinical testing infrastructure, a recurring-revenue pharma services market far larger than transplant hardware.
insights.quote: It gives us a living human organ model for translational research that no animal system can match, because the biology, the immunology, and the drug responses are human from the outset
insights.locator: 'Similar experiments can be done on livers'

insights.claim: US company Bexorg is reanimating human brains with perfusion pumps to study experimental drug effects, currently sustaining them for about a day and aiming to extend to two weeks, showing the research-platform use case is already being commercialized beyond livers.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Multiple organs and multiple startups chasing the same perfusion-as-testbed thesis signals a nascent category rather than a one-lab curiosity.

insights.claim: Pulitano speculates that because a living donor's split liver regrows to near-full volume in about two months, dividing a liver and attaching the sections to perfusion machines could multiply one donor liver into several full-size organs.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Organ multiplication would attack the supply constraint that caps the entire transplant market; it is the highest-optionality claim in the piece and the least evidenced.
insights.locator: 'In living donations, surgeons commonly take half'

insights.claim: Patents filed by billionaire-backed longevity startup Altos Labs describe introducing reprogramming genes into animal livers maintained outside the body, with scientists speculating about temporarily disconnecting a failing organ inside a patient to dose it with ultra-powerful genetic treatments without exposing the rest of the body.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Perfusion as an organ-isolated delivery route would relax the systemic-toxicity ceiling on aggressive gene therapies, a patent position worth tracking in the longevity space.
insights.locator: 'Meanwhile, in Silicon Valley, patents filed by Altos Labs'

insights.claim: Martins argues long-term organ life support could enable artificial wombs, new types of organ manufacturing, and extended direct experimentation on human organs outside the body, defending pursuit of capability ahead of demonstrated need.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: The field's own advocates justify the work on option value rather than current need, so expect funding to depend on narrative and societies rather than near-term clinical revenue.
insights.quote: It’s important to have people thinking outside the box and pushing the limits and creating possibilities for things that, right now, sometimes we don’t even have a need for but are going to be needed in the future
insights.locator: 'Yet that's where things could start to get interesting'

insights.claim: Two new scientific societies have formed around long-duration organ support: Martins' International Society for Organ Preservation and Perfusion Therapy, holding its inaugural meeting in Italy this year, and a China-based body launched in August by doctors at the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University to advance 'organ medicine' via 'bionic maintenance'.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
entities: International Society for Organ Preservation and Perfusion Therapy
First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
insights.so_what: Society formation is the standard early marker of a field becoming fundable and standards-setting; the parallel China track signals a second, state-adjacent center of gravity.
insights.locator: 'Doctors probing the limits of organ life support'

insights.claim: Pulitano characterizes the explosive growth as being in the concept that perfusion technology goes beyond organ preservation entirely, describing it as an entirely new category rather than an improvement to transplantation.
insights.speaker: Antonio Regalado
insights.so_what: Category creation narratives precede capital formation; treat 'organ medicine' as a label to watch across biotech funding rounds and patent filings.
insights.quote: What is exploding is the idea of this technology that clearly goes beyond simply organ preservation
insights.locator: Closing paragraph: 'What is exploding is the idea'

top_entities: International Society for Organ Preservation and Perfusion Therapy
First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
